# Supply: MESACLIP to the coupler

*Generated by Claude.*

DATM, DOCN and DICE read MESACLIP through XML stream definitions and send fields to the coupler.
This page covers what they send and how each field is made, the MESACLIP variables not used yet,
the stream time settings, the meshes, and where the XML comes from. Which fields the models ask
for, and which nobody supplies, is on the demand page,
[Demand: what the models import](stream_data_requirements.md). The files themselves are described
in [MESACLIP experiments](mesaclip_experiments.md#files-and-history-streams).

## Flags

Fields with no flag are read directly from MESACLIP, at most with a unit conversion, or come from
somewhere else, as the tables say.

- {bdg-info}`computed`: calculated in the `mesaclip` datamode from other MESACLIP variables.
- {bdg-primary}`h4`: read from `cam.h4`, the 6-hourly means. All other atmosphere fields come from
  the `cam.h2` 6-hourly snapshots. Radiation (`FLDS`, `FSDS`, `SOLSD`, `SOLLD`) and the
  precipitation components (`PRECC`, `PRECSC`, `PRECSL`) are only saved in h4. `PRECT` is in both
  and is read from h4, so the rain/snow split uses a total and components averaged over the same
  window. Their time settings are under [stream parameters](#stream-parameters).

## From MESACLIP to the coupler

Every field the MESACLIP datamodes send to the coupler, and how each is made. GDEX files hold one
variable each, so there is one stream per variable, and each stream's `<var>` is
`name_in_file name_in_model`. Atmosphere variables come from `cam.h2` unless flagged {bdg-primary}`h4`,
ocean variables from `pop.h.nday1`, ice from `cice.h1`. Line links go to the datamode source.
Ice and ocean names were checked in HIST member 010's daily files only.

### DATM

| Coupler field | Meaning | How it's made | From MESACLIP | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Sa_u`, `Sa_v` | Lowest-level wind, zonal and meridional | direct | `UBOT`, `VBOT` | [273–274](datm:L273-L274) |
| `Sa_z` | Height of the lowest atmosphere level | direct | `ZBOT` | [268](datm:L268) |
| `Sa_tbot` | Lowest-level air temperature | direct | `TREFHT` | [269](datm:L269) |
| `Sa_shum` | Lowest-level specific humidity | direct | `QREFHT` | [270](datm:L270) |
| `Sa_pbot` | Lowest-level pressure | direct | `PS` | [271](datm:L271) |
| `Sa_pslv` | Sea-level pressure | direct | `PSL` | [272](datm:L272) |
| `Faxa_lwdn` | Downward longwave | direct | `FLDS` {bdg-primary}`h4` | [293](datm:L293) |
| `Faxa_swvdf` | Downward shortwave, visible diffuse | direct | `SOLSD` {bdg-primary}`h4` | [295](datm:L295) |
| `Faxa_swndf` | Downward shortwave, near-IR diffuse | direct | `SOLLD` {bdg-primary}`h4` | [294](datm:L294) |
| `Sa_ptem` | Lowest-level potential temperature | = `Sa_tbot`: CAM's T (ps/p)^κ ([CAM](https://github.com/ESCOMP/CAM/blob/cam6_4_187/src/control/camsrfexch.F90#L496)) with p = `PS` | `TREFHT` | [279](datm:L279) |
| `Sa_u10m`, `Sa_v10m` | 10 m wind, zonal and meridional | copy of `Sa_u`, `Sa_v` (~60 m winds) | `UBOT`, `VBOT` | [283–284](datm:L283-L284) |
| `Faxa_snowc` | Convective snow | unit conversion, m/s → kg/m²/s | `PRECSC` {bdg-primary}`h4` | [291](datm:L291) |
| `Faxa_snowl` | Large-scale snow | unit conversion, m/s → kg/m²/s | `PRECSL` {bdg-primary}`h4` | [292](datm:L292) |
| `Sa_dens` | Lowest-level air density | {bdg-info}`computed` | `PS` / (Rd `TREFHT` (1 + zvir `QREFHT`)) | [280](datm:L280) |
| `Faxa_rainc` | Convective rain | {bdg-info}`computed` | (`PRECC` − `PRECSC`) × 1000 {bdg-primary}`h4` | [289](datm:L289) |
| `Faxa_rainl` | Large-scale rain | {bdg-info}`computed` | (`PRECT` − `PRECC` − `PRECSL`) × 1000 {bdg-primary}`h4` | [290](datm:L290) |
| `Faxa_swvdr` | Downward shortwave, visible direct | {bdg-info}`computed` | (`FSDS` − `SOLSD` − `SOLLD`) × 0.475 {bdg-primary}`h4` | [297](datm:L297) |
| `Faxa_swndr` | Downward shortwave, near-IR direct | {bdg-info}`computed` | (`FSDS` − `SOLSD` − `SOLLD`) × 0.525 {bdg-primary}`h4` | [298](datm:L298) |
| `Sa_topo` | Surface height (topography) | DATM's observed topography stream | — | [267](datm:L267) |

Direct shortwave is split between visible and near-IR in JRA's 0.28 : 0.31 ratio.

**Read but not sent to the coupler:** the stream fields `Faxa_swdn` (`FSDS`), `Faxa_prect`,
`Faxa_precc`, `Faxa_precsc` and `Faxa_precsl` are only inputs to the computed fields above.

### DOCN

| Coupler field | Meaning | How it's made | From MESACLIP | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `So_t` | Sea-surface temperature | unit conversion, °C → K | `SST` | [198–200](docn:L198-L200) |
| `So_s` | Sea-surface salinity | unit conversion, kg/kg → g/kg (= psu) | `SSS` | [182](docn:L182) |
| `So_u`, `So_v` | Surface current, zonal and meridional | unit conversion, cm/s → m/s; not rotated | `U1_1`, `V1_1` | [156](docn:L156), [163](docn:L163) |
| `So_omask` | Ocean fraction of each cell | ocean fraction of the model mesh | — | [134](docn:L134) |
| `So_bldepth` | Ocean boundary-layer depth | 0, no stream: MESACLIP has no daily mean (WW3 floors it at 5 m) | — | [174](docn:L174) |

`SSS` files hold kg/kg although their units attribute says g/kg. Without the stream, `So_s` is
34.7 psu, as DOCN%SST sends. CICE uses it, and DICE uses it for the freezing point. Currents stay
on POP's grid axes ([meshes and remapping](#meshes-and-remapping)).

### DICE

Only `Si_ifrac` and `Si_thick` come from MESACLIP. DICE makes everything else itself, from the ice fraction and
the fields it imports from DATM and the ocean, as DICE%SSMI does.

| Coupler field | Meaning | How it's made | From MESACLIP | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Si_ifrac` | Ice fraction | unit conversion, % → fraction, clipped to 0–1¹ | `aice_d` | [418](dice:L418), [458](dice:L458), [521–529](dice:L521-L529) |
| `Si_thick` | Ice thickness (for WW3) | `hi_d` ÷ ice fraction where there is ice, else 0, as CICE does | `hi_d`, `aice_d` | [423–428](dice:L423-L428) |
| `Si_imask` | Ice mask | ice mask of the model mesh | — | [251](dice:L251) |
| `Si_t` | Ice surface temperature | made up: 260 ± 10 K seasonal cycle, pulled toward freezing | — | [461–465](dice:L461-L465), [539](dice:L539) |
| `Si_avsdr`, `Si_anidr`, `Si_avsdf`, `Si_anidf` | Ice albedo, 4 bands | fixed albedos | — | [468–471](dice:L468-L471) |
| `Faii_swnet` | Net shortwave into the ice | DATM's 4 bands × (1 − albedo) | via DATM | [476–479](dice:L476-L479) |
| `Faii_*` (6 fields), `Si_tref`, `Si_qref` | Ice-atmosphere fluxes and stress; 2 m T, q | bulk formula from DATM and `Si_t` | via DATM | [543–548](dice:L543-L548) |
| `Fioi_melth`, `Fioi_meltw` | Melt heat, meltwater | from the ocean's `Fioo_q` and ice fraction | — | [482–535](dice:L482-L535) |
| `Fioi_swpen` | Shortwave through the ice | `flux_swpf` (default 0) × `Faii_swnet` | — | [562](dice:L562) |
| `Fioi_taux`, `Fioi_tauy` | Ice-ocean stress | = `Faii_taux`, `Faii_tauy` | — | [565–566](dice:L565-L566) |
| `Fioi_salt` | Salt flux, ice to ocean | 0 | — | [569](dice:L569) |
| `Fioi_bcpho`, `Fioi_bcphi`, `Fioi_flxdst` | Black carbon, dust to ocean | DATM's aerosol deposition | — | [575–578](dice:L575-L578) |
| `Si_ifrac_n`, `Fioi_swpen_ifrac_n` | Per-category ice fraction, shortwave | one category (per-category coupling only) | — | [584–585](dice:L584-L585) |

¹ With `flux_qacc` (on by default), `Si_ifrac` is at least 0.01 where there is ice, and new ice can
form where the ocean's freeze potential `Fioo_q` builds up.

## MESACLIP variables not used yet

These are in the MESACLIP files ([variable glossary](mesaclip_experiments.md#variable-glossary)) but
not in any stream, and could replace a stand-in, a made-up value or a missing field:

| MESACLIP variable | Meaning | File | Could provide | Instead of |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `U10` | 10 m wind speed | `cam.h2` | rescaled `Sa_u10m`, `Sa_v10m` | ~60 m winds |
| `XBLT` | Daily maximum boundary-layer depth | `pop.h.nday1` | `So_bldepth` (biased deep) | 0 |
| `SSH_2` | Sea-surface height | `pop.h.nday1` | `So_dhdx`, `So_dhdy` from its gradient² | not supplied |
| `Tsfc_d` | Snow/ice surface temperature | `cice.h1` | `Si_t` | DICE's made-up seasonal value |
| `fswthru_d` | Shortwave through the ice to the ocean | `cice.h1` | `Fioi_swpen` | 0 |

² Needs preprocessing on the tripole grid.

The rest are diagnostics no model imports: upper-air fields (`T200`, `U250`, `Z500`, …), clear-sky
and net radiation, turbulent fluxes CMEPS computes itself (`LHFLX`, `SHFLX`, `TAUX`, …), and the
coupler flux diagnostics in `pop.h.nday1` (`*_F`).

## Stream parameters

The time settings depend on the history file. Tag meanings are in the
[CDEPS streams docs](https://escomp.github.io/CDEPS/versions/master/html/streams.html).

| Tag | cam.h2 | cam.h4 | pop.h.nday1 | cice.h1 |
|-----|--------|--------|-------------|---------|
| `taxmode` | `limit` | `limit` | `limit` | `limit` |
| `tintalgo` | `linear` | `nearest` | `nearest` | `nearest` |
| `offset` (s) | `0` | `-10800` | `-43200` | `-43200` |
| `readmode` | `single` | `single` | `single` | `single` |
| `dtlimit` | `1.e30` | `1.e30` | `1.e30` | `1.e30` |

**`tintalgo` and `offset`:** `cam.h2` fields are snapshots (no `cell_methods`),
so they are interpolated linearly. `cam.h4`, `pop.h.nday1` and `cice.h1` fields
are means (`cell_methods = "time: mean"`) stamped at the end of their window
(`time_bnds` upper bound equals `time`). A negative offset of half a window moves
each stamp to the middle of its window, and `nearest` then picks the mean whose
window contains the model time.

**Years:** `year_first` and `year_last` are `DATM_YR_START` and `DATM_YR_END`, which default to
the scenario's whole data range, and `year_align` equals `year_first`. So model years are data
years, and a run can start anywhere inside the range.

**`taxmode`:** `limit` stops the run if the model time leaves
`year_first`–`year_last`, instead of wrapping around (`cycle`) or holding the end
values (`extend`). Keep `year_first` at the dataset's first year, not the run's,
so a 1950 start is inside the data. A run starting on a dataset's first day
(e.g. RCP runs on 2006-01-01) is before the first daily record (00:00 on
2 January) and stops; start it on 2 January or use `extend` for that run.

**`dtlimit`:** `1.e30` turns off CDEPS's check for gaps in the time axis, so a
missing file is interpolated across without an error. `add_mesaclip_to_cesm.py`
reports missing files per member.

## Meshes and remapping

| History files | Mesh | `mapalgo` |
|---|---|---|
| `cam.h2`, `cam.h4` | `share/meshes/ne120np4_ESMFmesh_cdf5_c20211018.nc` | `bilinear` |
| `pop.h.nday1`, `cice.h1` | `share/meshes/tx0.1v2_ESMFmesh_cd5_c20210105.nc` | `bilinear` |

Mesh paths are under CESM inputdata. The WW3 mesh is set in WW3, not in these streams.

**Winds** need no rotation: CAM-SE's `UBOT` and `VBOT` are already east/north.

**Currents** are not yet rotated. POP's `U1_1` and `V1_1` follow the tripole grid's axes, which
match east/north south of about 29°N and turn by up to 90° in the Arctic. They also sit on U
points but are read on the T-point mesh. The streams' `vectors` tag can't fix this: CDEPS
assumes vector input is already east/north and rotates by longitude only
(`dshr_strdata_mod.F90`).

## Where the stream XML comes from

`code/claude/mesaclip.py` holds the tables on this page: scenarios, history files and their time
settings, and the field mapping. `code/claude/add_mesaclip_to_cesm.py` writes them into CDEPS's
`stream_definition_{datm,docn,dice}.xml`, with `$DATM_MESACLIP_CASE` in every file path and
`$DATM_YR_START`/`END`/`ALIGN` for the years. The case's namelist build fills those in. Every
file is listed, because GDEX file names hold date ranges that CDEPS can't template.

`code/claude/generate_{datm,docn,dice}_streams.py` write blank CPLHIST-style templates and hold the
lists of fields each data model must supply. The MESACLIP modes don't use their output.
